newsitem.title: UK: UKI PMI index rise to 2-year high of 54.6 in May.
newsitem.headline: UKI PMI index rise to 2-year high of 54.6 in May.

text.p: British manufacturing expanded for the 12th month in a row in May and the purchasing managers' index (PMI) rose to a seasonally adjusted 54.6, its highest level since April 1995, from 53.6 in April, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
"Manufacturers again increased output to meet substantial growth in orders," the CIPS said.

"Buoyant domestic demand from consumers continued to boost order books. Despite a further fall in the rate of growth of export orders, attributed to the sustained strength of the pound, UK manufacturers experienced the fastest growth of total orders since last November."
The survey, sponsored by Reuters, showed manufacturers increased production for the 12th consecutive month, provoking further growth in the quantity of goods purchased.

"The rate of growth of goods purchased dipped slightly, however, and remained subdued relative to output growth as manufacturers continued to keep stock levels under control for cost considerations," the CIPS said.
The strong pound continued to adversely affect manufacturing exports but it again reduced the prices of imported materials.
The prices index signalled a further sharp fall in input prices, with a quarter of all manufacturers reporting a fall in prices from a month ago while only 7.5 percent reported a rise.

Suppliers' delivery times lengthened only slightly as suppliers have generally been able to meet rising demand without significant delays. Only nine percent of manufacturers reported lengthening lead times in May.

"The ability of suppliers to meet existing demand and the continuing trend of low input prices has enabled an increasing number of firms to implement cost-cutting destocking policies. Stocks of purchases fell for the 25th month in a row."
The manufacturing workforce continued to grow but growth was relatively muted compared with accelerating growth in output and orders.
Following are the seasonally adjusted PMI indices, with originally reported March figures in brackets:
May April
Purchasing managers' index 54.6 53.6 (53.1)
Quantity of purchases 53.6 54.7 (55.3)
Suppliers' delivery times 49.7 49.5 (50.1)
Stocks of purchases 46.9 47.6 (47.6)
Stocks of finished goods 46.3 48.1 (48.1)
Employment 52.8 51.4 (51.2)

NOTE: The PMI is based on a weighted average of seasonally adjusted measures of output, new orders, suppliers' delivery times, stocks of items purchased and employment. A reading above 50 indicates that manufacturing is generally expanding, below 50 that it is generally contracting.
-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
